title: Monarch Health KVCache + 502 breadcrumb scratchpad
content:
Purpose: scratchpad for MONARCH-INCIDENT (INF-2148). Customer: Monarch Health (multi-tenant dedicated). Quick goal: capture commands, raw errors, hypotheses and a short draft to send to CSM.

Short summary (so far):
- 2026-03-11 morning: Monarch reported intermittent 502s for batch text-generation calls across sessions tied to a single dedicated pool (us-west-2). Errors spike ~09:15-09:45 PST. Throughput normal otherwise.
- Appears correlated with model reload events (we triggered rolling restart for a perf patch at ~02:00 UTC) but customer says first saw it before our restart (notes below).

Timeline (raw):
- 2026-03-11 08:57 PST — first alert from Customer -> CSM
- 2026-03-11 09:05 PST — infra-alert: elevated 502 rate from gateway -> SRE
- 2026-03-11 09:12 PST — I SSH'd into control-plane-console to check routing and model assignments
- 2026-03-11 09:18 PST — observed repeated socket hangups between proxy and worker
- 2026-03-11 09:33 PST — applied temporary routing rule to fall back to model-variant v2b (reduced error rate)
- 2026-03-12 11:20 PST — follow-up: reproducible when sending long-context requests (>1024 tokens) with KV cache enabled

Commands I ran (keepsafe copy):
- kubectl checks:
  kubectl get pods -n dedicated-monarch -o wide
  kubectl describe pod monarch-infer-0 -n dedicated-monarch
  kubectl logs monarch-infer-0 -n dedicated-monarch -c inference --since=1h | tail -n 120

- sample logs (trimmed):
  "2026-03-11T09:17:42Z ERROR inference-proxy: upstream_response: 502 Bad Gateway (socket hang up) at proxy.go:142"
  "2026-03-11T09:17:42Z WARN batcher: drop_request: queue_full session=abc123 size=64"
  "2026-03-11T09:17:43Z ERROR runtime: KVCache: missing chunk(s) for session=abc123 expected=3 got=0"
  "2026-03-11T09:17:44Z ERROR worker: model inference failed: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed"
  "2026-03-11T09:17:45Z ERROR runtime: failed to allocate tensor: OOM allocating 16777216 bytes"

- docker/container level checks:
  kubectl exec -it monarch-infer-0 -n dedicated-monarch -c inference -- bash -c 'nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,memory.used --format=csv'
  # output: GPU 98%, Memory 86%, mem used=25.3GiB (one worker at near capacity)

- control plane / router checks:
  curl -s -X GET "https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/pools/monarch/assignments" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq .
  # saw a mix of worker variants: model-v2b (quantized) and model-v2a (full fp16) both assigned

- kvcache introspection (redis on dedicated cluster):
  redis-cli -h redis-monarch-1 info | head
  redis-cli -h redis-monarch-1 LRANGE kvcache:sessions:abc123 0 -1
  # observed empty list for some sessions, but keys exist for others

What I changed / mitigations tried:
- 09:33 PST: rolled traffic off model-v2a -> model-v2b (temporary)
- 09:46 PST: lowered batcher max_wait_ms from 40 -> 20 (to reduce queue buildup)
- 10:10 PST: increased per-worker max-concurrent-requests from 8 -> 12 to attempt headroom (may have worsened OOMs)
- 10:28 PST: gated huge-context requests (>1024) to force client-side truncation for Monarch to stop immediate failures

Hypotheses (not mutually exclusive):
1) KV cache invalidation bug after model reload: workers reloaded weights and cleared shards unevenly; router still believes sessions are warm and sends KV headers -> worker replies with missing chunks -> runtime errors -> proxy treats as upstream failure -> 502.
   Evidence: "KVCache: missing chunk(s)" logs, some sessions return empty LRANGE.
2) Mixed model variant compatibility: router sends requests to quantized (v2b) vs fp16 (v2a) workers interchangeably; serialization of KV cache differs slightly and leads to deserialization errors on some workers. Evidence: assignments show both variants.
3) Batcher overload with long-context requests: large prefix length causes huge KV transfers and batcher queue to fill -> drop_request logs -> connection resets. Evidence: batcher: drop_request logs and high GPU mem usage.
4) Envoy/keepalive mismatch causing socket hangups under high throughput when workers GC/oom. Evidence: upstream 'socket hang up' at proxy.go and worker 'connection closed'.

Repro steps (how I can trigger locally):
- synthetic load with long context (1k-2k tokens) using monarch model-variant v2a:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer test" -d '{"model":"monarch:v2a","input":"<repeat 1000 token chunk>","max_tokens":512,"use_kv":true}'
- run while toggling worker to perform rolling restart; watch for KV cache inconsistencies in redis

Back-of-envelope impact: ~3-5% of requests to this pool returned 502 during the ~30m window; most are long-context generation flows used by Monarch's clinical note stitching job.

Open questions / next actions:
- Confirm whether model-variant serialization format changed between v2a and v2b (ask model-onboarding team).
- Add additional KVCache guards: if missing chunks, fall back to cold-run (recompute) rather than failing the request.
- Add improved metrics: #missing-kv-chunks / requests, per-session kv chunk count histogram.
- Consider sticky routing for sessions until KVCache warm-confirmed.

Draft internal note to CSM / Monarch (short):
Hi Jamie,

Short apology and summary: we looked into the 502s you saw on 2026-03-11. Early root cause looks like an interaction between the session KV cache and mixed worker variants in your dedicated pool, which caused intermittent missing cache chunks for long-context requests. That in turn caused worker RPC failures and upstream 502 responses.

What we did: temporarily routed traffic to the quantized variant (v2b) to reduce errors, gated very long requests, and are rolling a fix to avoid failing on missing KV chunks.

Next steps: engineering will (a) add a safe fallback when KV chunks are missing (b) ensure routing is sticky while cache is re-warming (c) follow up with a production-ready patch and postmortem. Expect a status update by EOD tomorrow.

If you want immediate relief we can schedule a coordinated restart of your pool off-hours or pin traffic to the variant we validated — let me know preference.

-- Leah

Draft external-facing timeline (for email/postmortem): keep short, only after RCA.

Notes to self: tag INF-2148, add unit test for kv serialization compatibility between fp16 and int8 quantized runtimes, follow up with @Sofia about redis shard metrics, ping model-onboarding on compatibility matrix.

Slack snippets for IR channel (copy/paste):
- "MONARCH: observed KVCache missing-chunk errors during high long-context load. rolling routing -> v2b reduced errors. Investigating serialization / cache invalidation. INF-2148"
- "cmds: kubectl logs monarch-infer-0 -c inference | grep KVCache | tail -n 50"

Random notes / fragments:
- When we bumped max-concurrent-requests to 12 it increased OOMs -> revert if needed.
- Consider decreasing worker-side default batch size for long-context jobs.
- Check PR #762 for the perf patch that triggered rolling restarts (might include minor model artifact rename)

--- end of scratchpad ---
